why.emptyGroup: is an empty group, which matches nothing

bind.noValueIgnored: {{word}}: has no value and was ignored
bind.valueNotScope: {{word}}: takes a value, not curly brackets
bind.countsRows: {{head}}{{value}} is read as a count — spells with {{value}} {{label}}
bind.negatedRowCount: a minus before a count is not read — turn the comparison round instead, as in {{word}}<=2

axis.noOrdering: {{word}} has no order to sort by
axis.takes: not a value {{word}} can take — it takes {{hint}}
axis.takesQuoted: a quoted value is text, and {{word}} takes {{hint}}
axis.noRegex: {{word}} cannot take a regular expression — they run on text and file names only

pattern.pathWeak: a regular expression on a file name rarely helps — file names run their words together
pattern.unclosed: the regular expression has no closing / — it ends at the first space, so a space is written \s

value.differentQuestions: these alternatives cannot be searched together
value.glued: two values run together — a space is missing
value.exactPattern: = cannot combine with a regular expression
value.anchorPattern: {{symbol}} cannot combine with a regular expression
value.trailingRange: {{written}} reads as at least {{bound}} — the same as {{wildcard}} for the upper bound
value.punctuationOnly: punctuation alone cannot be searched — search it as a regular expression

scope.innerBindScope: inside curly brackets a field takes a value, not more curly brackets
scope.twoKinds: {{a}} and {{b}} are two different kinds, so no single {{column}} is both
scope.nested: curly brackets cannot hold more curly brackets
scope.unclosedBeforeNext: the { was never closed — it is read as closed before the next field
scope.unclosedAtEnd: the { was never closed — it is read as closed at the end
scope.needsPositive: curly brackets need something to look for — a minus only narrows
scope.contentNegation: both are plain words, which rarely describe the same thing — exclude a kind or a property instead
scope.qualifierAlone: {{name}} only says who it plays on — add what it is
scope.foreignAxis: {{word}} is not a {{column}} field, so it cannot go inside {{column}}'s curly brackets

fix.ownClause: move it out on its own
fix.asPattern: search it as a regular expression

simplify.allDead: every alternative of this query contradicts itself; it is returned as written
simplify.matchesEverything: this query matches every spell — one alternative selects whatever the other excludes — so its simplest form is the empty query

sort.takesDoor: {{word}} takes a field to order by, as in {{word}}{{bind}}name or {{word}}{{bind}}{{negate}}model
sort.takesCount: {{word}} takes how many to list, as in {{word}}{{bind}}20
